findings.title: GET request uses full URI as request target, breaking URLs with query strings
findings.evidence: The request is constructed as 'Net::HTTP::Get.new(uri)'. In Net::HTTP, requests sent over an origin-form connection should use the path/query target, not the absolute URI object; for common inputs like 'https://example.com/search?q=x', this can produce an invalid or unexpected request target and fail against normal servers.
findings.recommendation: Build the request from the request URI instead, e.g. use 'Net::HTTP::Get.new(uri.request_uri)' or 'Net::HTTP::Get.new(uri.request_uri, headers)' so the path and query are sent correctly for standard HTTPS origin requests.
